title: Homework-2
text:
Suppose we have data from a medical experiment on blood pressure. We have the following pre-treatment values for subjects 1 through 20:

130, 128, 116, 124, 133, 134, 118, 126, 114, 127, 141, 138, 128, 140, 137, 131, 120, 128, 139, 135

after treatment, the subjects were measured again (subjects 1 through 20 match)

114, 98, 113, 99, 107, 116, 113, 111, 119, 117, 101, 119, 130, 122, 106, 106, 124, 102, 117, 113


Create two vectors. One vector corresponding to the pre measurements and one to the post measurements.

pre_tr <- c(130, 128, 116, 124, 133, 134, 118, 126, 114, 127, 141, 138, 128, 140, 137, 131, 120, 128, 139, 135)

post_tr <- c(114, 98, 113, 99, 107, 116, 113, 111, 119, 117, 101, 119, 130, 122, 106, 106, 124, 102, 117, 113)

Assign names to the vector elements using the paste() function. Note that names() can be overwritten by a character vector. To quickly create the names, try running the code. Create the same names for each vector’s elements.

subject_names <- paste("Subject", 1:20, sep = "_")

names(pre_tr) <- subject_names
names(post_tr) <- subject_names

Calculate the change in blood pressure for each patient by subtracting post-treatment measurements from pre-treatment measurements. Recall that R does math element-wise! Save this calculation as a new object (also a vector).

change_tr <- pre_tr - post_tr
change_tr

 Subject_1  Subject_2  Subject_3  Subject_4  Subject_5  Subject_6  Subject_7 
        16         30          3         25         26         18          5 
 Subject_8  Subject_9 Subject_10 Subject_11 Subject_12 Subject_13 Subject_14 
        15         -5         10         40         19         -2         18 
Subject_15 Subject_16 Subject_17 Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20 
        31         25         -4         26         22         22 


Calculate the average decrease in blood pressure across all patients.

avg_change <- mean(change_tr)
avg_change

[1] 17


The average of all 20 patients the blood pressure dropped by 17 points.
Determine which patients experienced a decrease in blood pressure after treatment (a positive change). Use the which() function to just return the indices (and names) associated with this type of change.

decreased_tr <- which(change_tr > 0)
decreased_tr

 Subject_1  Subject_2  Subject_3  Subject_4  Subject_5  Subject_6  Subject_7 
         1          2          3          4          5          6          7 
 Subject_8 Subject_10 Subject_11 Subject_12 Subject_14 Subject_15 Subject_16 
         8         10         11         12         14         15         16 
Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20 
        18         19         20 


Based on the output, we can see how subjects 9,13, and 17 are not part of the list, indicating that their blood pressure went up after the treatment. Thus, the treatment didn’t help them.
Subset the vector of differences to only return those that have a positive change.

decreased_changes_tr <- change_tr[decreased_tr]
decreased_changes_tr 

 Subject_1  Subject_2  Subject_3  Subject_4  Subject_5  Subject_6  Subject_7 
        16         30          3         25         26         18          5 
 Subject_8 Subject_10 Subject_11 Subject_12 Subject_14 Subject_15 Subject_16 
        15         10         40         19         18         31         25 
Subject_18 Subject_19 Subject_20 
        26         22         22 


In this case we know that subjects 9, 13 and 17 are the patients whose blood pressure went up after the treatment.
Calculate the average decrease in blood pressure for those where the blood pressure decreased (positive change).

avg_change_decreased <- mean(decreased_changes_tr)
avg_change_decreased

[1] 20.64706


Comparing the two resulted averages, notice how when we included everyone, the average decreased by 17, however this resulted included 3 patients whose blood pressure did not decrease. After we calculated the average only including the 17 patients who blood pressure improved, the average decreases about 20.65 points. This results is more accurate to identify the effectiveness of the treatment.

Task 3: List Practice
Suppose we now also have data from another experiment where the ‘treatment’ was actually a placebo. We have the following pre-treatment values for subjects 1 through 10 (different set of subjects):

138, 135, 147, 117, 152, 134, 114, 121, 131, 130

after treatment, the subjects were measured again (subjects 1 through 10 match)

105, 136, 123, 130, 134, 143, 135, 139, 120, 124


Create a new data frame with this data in it that is similar to the data frame from task 2 (including the new column).

pre_tr_pl <- c(138, 135, 147, 117, 152, 134, 114, 121, 131, 130)
post_tr_pl <-c(105, 136, 123, 130, 134, 143, 135, 139, 120, 124)

patient_pl <- 1:10
diff_pl <- pre_tr_pl - post_tr_pl

bp_df_pl <- data.frame(patient = patient_pl,
                       pre_bp  = pre_tr_pl,
                       post_bp = post_tr_pl,
                       diff_bp = diff_pl,
                       row.names = NULL)

bp_df_pl$post_under_120 <- bp_df_pl$post_bp < 120

title: Homework-2
text:
Task 4: Control Flow Practice

Suppose we want to characterize the post-treatment (or placebo) blood pressure measurement as optimal (≤ 120), borderline (120 < bp ≤ 130), and high (> 130). First, create a new column in each data frame from above called status. You can do this via
your_df$status <- character(20) #or 10 depending on number of observations
Note: You want to add this additional column to the data frames that are stored in your list (R doesn’t do referencing to the original object).

experiment_list$treatment$status <- character(nrow(experiment_list$treatment))
experiment_list$placebo$status <- character(nrow(experiment_list$placebo))

For the non-placebo data frame (within the list), create a for loop and use if/then/else logic to create the status column’s values.

for (i in 1:nrow(experiment_list$treatment)) {
  bp_value <- experiment_list$treatment$post_bp[i]
  if (bp_value <= 120) {
    experiment_list$treatment$status[i] <- "optimal"
  } else if (bp_value > 120 & bp_value <= 130) {
    experiment_list$treatment$status[i] <- "borderline"
  } else {
    experiment_list$treatment$status[i] <- "high"
  }
}
